summary: At just three square miles with over 53,000 residents packed in at nearly 17,750 per square mile, Huntington Park is one of the most densely populated cities in the entire United States — denser than San Francisco on a per-square-mile basis. That intensity shows up on the ground: this is flat, fully built-out southeastern Los Angeles County, with virtually no undeveloped land, minimal open space, and a street grid that functions more like a compressed urban core than a suburb. Pacific Boulevard serves as the commercial spine, lined with small retailers and food counters that give the corridor a persistent sidewalk bustle unusual for cities this size. The affordability math, though, is tighter than it first appears — a median home value near $558,000 against a median household income of roughly $57,000 yields a price-to-income ratio above 9.5, making ownership a steep climb; median rent of $1,440 is more manageable but still claims about 30 percent of gross income. The climate is genuinely pleasant year-round, averaging 76°F daytime highs and 9.4 hours of sunshine daily, though the flat topography and surrounding industrial corridors along the adjacent rail lines and freight infrastructure mean air quality varies block to block. Motor vehicle theft runs notably high at 1,490 per 100,000, a figure worth weighing. Huntington Park is fundamentally a working city — small-footprint, commerce-heavy, and transit-connected via Metro bus lines — where density is the defining feature, not a side effect.
